why_how.text: Some conditions call for more following space, and the handbook suggests a four-second interval in these situations.
On slippery roads, leave more space ahead because stopping requires more distance.
When a following driver wants to pass, slow enough to create room ahead and help the pass finish sooner.
Give a motorcycle extra following room so a fallen rider can be avoided.
Motorcycles are especially likely to fall on wet, icy, gravel or metal surfaces such as bridge gratings and tracks.
Fall back when following a truck, bus, van or towing vehicle whose driver may not see you directly behind it.
A heavy load or trailer increases stopping distance, so leave more following room.
Increase the following gap when darkness or bad weather makes the view ahead difficult.
When closely followed, slow to encourage a pass or use a turnout to let the other driver by.
Allow emergency vehicles extra operating room when following them.
Approaching a railroad crossing, leave extra room behind buses or hazardous-material vehicles that must stop there.
When stopped on a hill, leave room for the vehicle ahead to roll backward as it starts.
A steady speed and early slowing signals help the driver behind maintain space.
For passenger pickup or drop-off, try to stop safely outside the traffic stream.
Before parallel parking with traffic approaching from behind, signal, draw alongside the space and let following vehicles pass.
If necessary slow driving holds up other cars, pull aside safely and let them pass.
If a tailgater follows and a right lane is available, move into that lane.
Without a right lane, wait for a clear way and reduce speed gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.
Do not brake suddenly to discourage a tailgater, because that increases rear-impact risk.
Avoid remaining beside other vehicles on a multilane road; move ahead or fall behind to keep side room.
On a two-lane road, avoid crowding the centerline and generally travel near the middle of your lane.
On a road with at least two lanes, move over for entering traffic if the adjacent lane is unoccupied.
Leave extra space beside parked vehicles because a person or vehicle may move into your path.

narration.text: Sounding the horn while approaching or passing a horse is illegal. Sounding the horn while approaching or passing a horse is illegal. Give extra room or exercise extra caution when another road user appears distracted. Treat unfamiliar, unexplained slowing or sign-searching drivers as potentially confused and leave room. If someone passes without enough room, slow to help that driver return safely rather than worsening the mistake. If another driver must change lanes suddenly, slow to allow a merge. Horseback riders are governed and protected by road rules and must ride single file near the right edge or on a usable right shoulder, lane or path.
